title: fix: stop cross-thread flag from mislabeling valid XML as invalid

contextNote: Fixes a concurrency bug where XML validity was gated on a process-global parse-error flag, so one thread's malformed parse could mislabel another thread's valid document as invalid; validity now comes from each thread's own parse result.
originalBody:
Decides XML validity from each thread's own parse result instead of a shared flag. `IsValidXML` gated its return on a process-global parse-error flag in addition to its own parse, so under concurrent execution one thread's failed parse of a malformed document could poison another thread's check of a valid one.

## Issue

`XMLUtils::IsValidXML` returned `xml_doc.IsValid() && !xml_parse_error_occurred`. That flag is a process-global `static bool`, not `thread_local`, and `XMLDocRAII` sets it whenever any thread's parse fails. When `read_xml`/`xml_valid` run across multiple workers (`PRAGMA threads > 1`), a malformed input on one thread can flip the flag while another thread is validating a well-formed document, so the valid document is reported as `File X contains invalid XML`. With `ignore_errors=false` the scan aborts; with `ignore_errors=true` the row is silently dropped. Serial execution never trips it.

## Changes

- `IsValidXML` now returns validity from this thread's own parse result only (`doc != nullptr`). The XML parser runs without `XML_PARSE_RECOVER`, so malformed input always yields a null document, making the flag redundant for detection and harmful for concurrency.
- The global flag is left in place but is now write-only. I kept it to hold this change to one line of behavior; the dead state is removed in the follow-up below.

## Testing

Adds `test/sql/concurrency_invalid_xml_race.test`: under `PRAGMA threads=4` a single concurrent scan validates 100k rows alternating well-formed and malformed XML, tallying any valid row reported invalid and any malformed row reported valid. On `main` the valid-row count surfaces thousands of false negatives; with this change both counts are zero.

## Cleanup

Once this and the out-of-memory hardening (#84) land, the process-global libxml2 error state this PR stops reading is fully dead. A small follow-up removes it: the write-only `xml_parse_error_occurred` / `xml_parse_error_message`, the unregistered `XMLErrorHandler` / `XMLSilentErrorHandler` (and its stale forward declaration in `xml_schema_inference.cpp`), and the dead flag writes in the `XMLDocRAII` constructors. `XMLSilentSchemaErrorHandler` stays (still registered for schema validation) with only its dead write dropped.

I kept it separate so this PR remains a one-line behavior change, and because the dead writes sit next to #84's new resource-error detection, so a clean removal depends on both landing first. It stacks on top of both and will be opened as a follow-up once they merge.
